newsitem.title: UK: British beer exports in second quarter hit high.
newsitem.headline: British beer exports in second quarter hit high.

text.p: British beer exports broke records in the second quarter of 1996, hitting 69 million stg, according to the latest sector review of food, drink and tabacco industries by the Office for National Statistics.

The report, which showed performance up to the second quarter of 1996, added that beer exports for last year hit 183 million, the highest for five years. The latest quarterly figures show that strong trend continuing.
Wine sales also demonstrated some fizz, with total exports worth 59 million last year, doubling levels seen in 1990. Cider and sherry exports hit 15.3 million last year.
Exports of tobacco products grew five-fold compared with imports, said the report. In the second quarter of 1996 Britain's tobacco exports totalled 295 million compared with imports of 60 million.
Food is the one area where imports have exceeded exports for the last five years, with the latest statistics showing 82 million worth of exports compared with 154 million of imports.
Commenting on food pricing, the report added that UK output prices in the second quarter for bread, cakes and fresh pastries rose 37 percent over the value in 1990.
